attributes.nuance_translation: A way to express that something has been done in the past.

attributes.body:
たことがある is a set expression in Japanese that is used for saying that 'there has been a time that I have done (A)'.

The auxiliary verb た will be added to the verb indicating what you have done, followed by こと - が - ある. Like の, こと is regularly used for nominalization (creating a noun-like phrase). However, の cannot replace こと in this particular grammar pattern.

From these examples, we can see that ない (the negative equivalent of ある) may also be used, when you want to express that you have 'never' done something.

Caution

Just like English, many set phrases cannot be adjusted in Japanese (in the same way that こと cannot be swapped with の in this expression).

Fun Fact

In expressions where こと is followed by a verb phrase, の may not be used. When used for nominalization, の is almost always followed by a noun or adjective phrase. Here are some examples.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Have been / done たことがある

attributes.body: With a non-past verb, ことがある expresses that something happens occasionally or from time to time, similar to saying 'There are times when…' In contrast, たことがある uses the past tense to describe a completed experience. For example, 日本に行ったことがある means 'I've been to Japan.' It refers to something that has happened at least once, without implying it occurred repeatedly.

first_relatable.title: ことがある
first_relatable.meaning: Something is possible, Sometimes, Occasionally, There are times when

attributes.body: Both expressions describe past experiences but with different nuances. たことがある states that something has happened before, as in 日本に行ったことがある ('I've been to Japan'). たものだ adds a nostalgic tone and refers to things done regularly in the past, as in 子どもの頃、よくこの公園で遊んだものだ ('I often played at this park when I was a child').
